clue.text: Pre-nuptial celebrations touring Hastings, good time

indicators.note: a touring party moves around, so the letters that follow are moved around too

parts.note: the Sussex town, taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bachelor party goes on a trip around Hastings and has a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings is a seaside town in Sussex, a natural place for a pre-wedding trip, which hides that its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is the British name for a groom's bachelor party with his male friends before the wedding.

clue.text: Frame airline before start of hijack

parts.note: SAS is Scandinavian Airlines

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of hijack

explanation.surface: An airline is framed for a crime before a hijacking begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding wooden or metal frame holding the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: Mythical boat with freight first removed

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away from the word for freight

parts.note: cargo is goods carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: A legendary ship sails after its load has been unloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend, sailing to fetch the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Their country's champions — like Red Rum and Mon Mome

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who passionately support their own nation's independence or interests

definitions.text: like Red Rum and Mon Mome
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: horses that won the Grand National

explanation.surface: Patriots are compared to famous racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum and Mon Mome both won the Grand National, the famous British steeplechase usually just called the National, so in the setter's playful sense they are Nationalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Political patriots who champion their nation's cause, and humorously, winners of the Grand National horse race.

clue.text: Go and putt it there!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the traffic-light colour that means proceed
second meaning: the short-cut grass on a golf course where you putt

explanation.surface: A golfing companion urges a player to take the shot and sink the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour signalling drivers may proceed, and the closely mown area surrounding the hole in golf.

clue.text: Stop rats barring opening in gallery

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so the opening letter of the word for rats is left off

parts.note: rats are vermin

explanation.surface: A demand to keep rats out of an art gallery's opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's best-known art gallery; 'opening' looks like an exhibition launch but is the first letter to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, a synonym of the verb stop.

clue.text: Some miss Cameron (Con)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of miss and start of Cameron

explanation.surface: Someone misses David Cameron, the Conservative former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed (Con) looks like a party label for Cameron, the Conservative; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle or confidence trick, which is a synonym of a scam.

clue.text: Noble women tot up letters

parts.note: to tot up is to add up or count
esses are the letter S, spelt out in the plural

explanation.surface: Aristocratic ladies add up their correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A countess is a female aristocrat of an earl's or count's rank, hence noble women.

clue.text: Centre Point in Levant etc

parts.note: the centre is the middle
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Centre Point, the London tower block, is being placed in the Levant.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Point is a famous London skyscraper, which hides that the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant, the lands of the eastern Mediterranean, is one part of the region of south-west Asia so named.

clue.text: But do such tourists just look at eyesores?

definitions.text: But do such tourists just look at eyesores?

parts.note: surface reading: holidaymakers who visit famous attractions
setter's reading: 'a sight' also means an ugly thing, so people who view sights would be viewers of ugliness

explanation.surface: A wry question whether tourists only ever visit ugly places.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke turns on the phrase 'you look a sight', where a sight is something ugly; split the answer into its two halves to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists who visit the places of interest of a town are said to go sightseeing.

clue.text: Who, in France, has penny for pound?

parts.note: qui is French for who
d was the symbol for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: Someone asks who in France would swap a penny for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is British slang for a pound sterling, the currency unit.

clue.text: Al cryptically at local surgery

parts.note: setter's reading: the two letters A and L, as a cryptic solver sees them, sit in the very middle of a word for wellness
surface reading: a man called Al is visiting his neighbourhood doctor

explanation.surface: A man called Al is at his local doctor's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer cryptically: AL is the centre of HEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A health centre is a building where local doctors and nurses hold their surgeries for the community.

clue.text: Firm of less importance gets chance

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
incidental means minor or secondary

explanation.surface: A minor company is given an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Chance must be read as an adjective here, as in a chance meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincidental describes something happening by accident, so the noun chance is used in its sense of by chance.

clue.text: Attractive objects drawn to drink?

parts.note: setter's reading: things that attract iron, shaped like a rod
surface reading: alluring people who are pulled towards the pub

explanation.surface: Good-looking people who just can't resist a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Attractive means magnetic, and the things drawn to drink would be drawn to a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: These are straight rod-shaped magnets, objects that literally attract metal.

clue.text: Expert in many fields?

parts.note: surface reading: a polymath knowledgeable across many subjects
setter's reading: fields of crops, the farmland a soil scientist studies

explanation.surface: A description of an all-round expert with broad knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies soil management and crop production, so works in farm fields literally.

clue.text: Ease an age problem which touches Crete

indicators.note: a problem has to be worked out, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on soothing the troubles of old age, perhaps with a Cretan holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete lies at the southern edge of this arm of the Mediterranean, whose waters wash its northern shore.

clue.text: Raving Jesuit and patron of lost causes

indicators.note: raving means wild and out of control, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A frenzied Jesuit priest appears alongside a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link between the Jesuit and the patron, but it belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic tradition this apostle is invoked as the patron saint of desperate and lost causes.

clue.text: Cotton thread one's placed in heart of galleon

indicators.note: something placed in another thing ends up inside it
the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the three central letters of galleon
one is I, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Cotton yarn, together with one sailor, is stowed in the hold of a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth, tightly twisted cotton thread, used especially for stockings.

clue.text: Roam around with leading indigenous Polynesian

indicators.note: around suggests turning things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leading letter is the one at the front of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of indigenous

explanation.surface: Wandering about with a leading native islander of the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, so a Maori is a Polynesian.

clue.text: They melt and oddly increase with these drifting

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third and so on

parts.note: letters one, three, five and seven of increase

indicators.note: drifting things wander out of place, so those letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climate warning: polar ice melts and sea levels rise as it drifts away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice sheets are vast continental masses of glacial ice, which are shrinking as they melt with warming.

clue.text: Spooky tales — Nordic drama for Conservatives

parts.note: Ghosts is a play by the Norwegian dramatist Ibsen
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Creepy stories: a Scandinavian play staged for a Conservative audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost stories are tales of hauntings and the supernatural, meant to frighten the listener.

clue.text: Marsupial's time for bed

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, and the 's adds an S
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A kangaroo's bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time for bed' reads as one phrase, but bed alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch where birds settle to sleep, a bird's bed.

clue.text: Join in and act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: participate in an activity
second meaning: play a role in a show

explanation.surface: An invitation to get involved and perform.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to participate, and also to play a role in a stage production.

clue.text: See 22
Tops of Egyptian pyramids in colour film

indicators.note: the tops of words in a down answer are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Pyramid peaks shown in a Technicolor movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the pyramids are in a colour film; 'film' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, grand-scale movie, often historical, such as a sword-and-sandal blockbuster.

clue.text: Out most of Saturday getting to a toll-road in Europe

indicators.note: out can mean in error or out of place, so the letters go into a new order
most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: the day, taken as written before trimming
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Away most of the weekend, driving on a motorway with tolls on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like part of the trip; it signals the anagram, and 'to a' belongs to the fodder, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An autostrada is an Italian motorway, and most of them charge drivers tolls.

clue.text: Test debacle at home …

indicators.note: a debacle is a complete collapse, so the word before it falls to pieces and is rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match goes disastrously for the home side.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; a sett is a badger's burrow, its home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the underground den of a badger, so the animal's home.

clue.text: … which starts camp clearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place where people have newly settled
second meaning: the paying off of a debt or bill

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a test that ruins the opening of a camp clearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots and 'which starts' link to 26, whose answer is the opening of this one; the clue proper is the double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement can be a small colony of new inhabitants, and also the clearing of an account by payment.
